hypothesis: Explicit installed-electric versus actuator-ready wording can produce a bounded alternate retrieval query that improves recall without changing selection behavior.
why_now: Both control states occur in core cases, and Cycle 14 was infrastructure-inconclusive rather than evaluated.
expected_effect: Better retrieval of the requested electric-control state while preserving source-query reranking, fusion, and fallback.
expected_metric_gain: +3.3–6.7 pp hard-pass plausible; blind gain uncertain.
lesson_from_history: Additive canonicalization was the only accepted family; gating, reranking, selection, and index changes were neutral or harmful. Cycle 14's Qdrant failure does not disprove this hypothesis.
candidate_hypotheses: State-specific installed-electric versus actuator-ready retrieval expansion (selected).
plan_summary: Created and strict-validated proposal, specification, design, and implementation-only tasks in openspec/changes/cycle-15-actuation-intent-retrieval-expansion/.
